implementation: Admits float64 reductions and selects binary64 positive zero for empty inputs. Reuses existing row-major adjacent-pair tree, width-aware scratch allocation, strict float64 addition, continuation planner and task runtime. Float32 and integer lowering retain their existing paths.

numerical_contract.order: row-major balanced adjacent pairs; odd tails copied unchanged
numerical_contract.addition: strict IEEE binary64 nearest ties to even, separately rounded, canonical arithmetic NaNs
numerical_contract.singleton: unchanged element bits, including signed zero and NaN payloads

qualification.scope: 64 checks passed in the broad run, then both numeric capability tests passed after replacing an obsolete float64 reduction rejection with int16 rejection and positive float64 reduction admission. No production changes between runs. Not the full 323-test suite
coverage: ranks zero through three and empty axes
unchanged singleton signed zero, subnormal and signaling/quiet NaN payloads
8192 sampled APFloat operand pairs per nonzero rank plus boundary and longer trees
odd lengths and power-of-two neighbors through 32769 cells
row-major padded/displaced and non-square transposed views
immutable inputs and settled scratch across success/failure
eight-byte bounds, negative metadata, allocation failure and cancellation
ordinary, builtin-spawn, nested, aliased and cached worker calls
integer sibling fault recovery reuses owned tensor data
scheduler/invocation allocation injection positions 1-24 with 1/2/4 workers
worker cancellation, deadline, admission rejection, typed result impostor rejection and settled owners
float64 matmul and Metal remain rejected with preserved destination artifacts
